As specified, on the out-of-fold years 2019-2021, FP costs, in sample: +0.086 R per trade (+0.124 -> +0.210) and +14.8 R (395 -> 304 trades). It survives costs x1.5 (+0.081 R per trade, +15.5 R) and x2 (+0.080, +17.4 R), one-minute entry and exit delays (+0.076, +15.9 R), the 3-spread stop rule and the weekend-gap control (+0.059 to +0.086). It is causal. That is the optimistic figure.

Two things discount it:
- **The 2021 fold** (11.1 of the 14.8 R) skipped only because 2018 was in its training. Trained on the last one or two years it skips nothing: +0.025 to +0.028 R per trade and +3.7 to +4.7 R in total, and criterion (c) fails. A threshold frozen on 2018-2019 and applied to 2020-2021 gives +0.058 R per trade, +5.2 R over two years.
- **The search:** this was the single winner among the author's 109 primary variants. The chance that a variant with no real effect does this well is 5-11 % on the procedure-level null and 35-96 % on bootstrap-based corrections.

What I think is left: about +0.03 to +0.06 R per trade on this sleeve, roughly +4 to +9 R over 2019-2021 (1.5 to 3 R a year), with a real chance that it is zero. It removes about a quarter of the trades in high-volatility regimes and does not shrink losses (average loss -0.72 R). Spread over a portfolio of about 1,350 trades a year it is worth less than +0.005 R per trade, far from the 0.35 R the user is after. If carried forward, the 2022 rule is: skip an ETH brk72 signal when 3 x ATR24 is at least 478.3 bp of the price.

where_the_losses_come_from: Losses are full stops near -1 R, not a fat tail. Ten sleeves, entries 2018-02-01..2021-12-31, FP costs, 5,205 trades (my re-simulation): 2,864 lost (55 %), average loss -0.65 R, gross loss 1,853 R against a gross gain of 2,642 R (+788.6 R net). 1,337 losses at the initial stop made -1,358 R (73 % of the gross loss), 1,417 at the clock exit -432 R, 110 at donch4h's trailing stop -63 R. Only 16 of the 2,864 losses were worse than -1.1 R (worst -1.49 R), and the worst tenth of the losing trades makes 16 % of the gross loss: there is no 'one big loss' beyond the stop.

Sleeve by sleeve, the size of a loss is set by the rule's stop and clock (same window, FP): orb_asia gold -0.99 R per losing trade (319 losers, 94 % of them full stops, 98 % of its gross loss); ocm4 -0.90 R (291; 83 %, 93 %); brk72 and F1 on btc and eth -0.73 to -0.74 R (260-300 losers each; 55-61 % full stops, 76-84 % of the gross loss); donch4h -0.59 R (115, mostly the trailing stop); noise30 -0.44 R (481, 405 at its band or clock exit); nq_btc_follow -0.37 R (451, 377 at its 60-minute clock); GOLD_FRI_PM -0.16 R (96, never stopped), and flat overall: -0.007 R per trade, -1.3 R on 183 trades.

The gains come from a few large winners: the best 5 % of the trades carry 144 % of the ten sleeves' total R (orb gold 548 %, ocm4 196 %, noise30 156 %, nq 135 %, crypto breakouts 89-108 %); without them the portfolio loses. The median winner peaks at +1.2 R and closes at +0.65 R.

The user's first claim does not hold on these rules: cutting at once a trade that starts hard the wrong way loses money. 19 % of the winners (439 trades, 2018-02..2021-12, FP) first went at least 0.5 R against them; together they made +577 R, 73 % of the ten sleeves' total (ocm4: 37 % of its winners, +89 R; orb gold: 40 %, +106 R; F1 btc: 26 %, +97 R). The quick check (all in-sample years, 7,965 trades, FP): closing a trade that shows -0.25 R or worse after 5, 15, 30, 60 or 120 minutes costs 98, 231, 180, 84 and 68 R (574 to 930 trades cut, 131 to 211 future winners killed); at -0.5 R it costs 4 to 28 R; only at -0.75 R does it sometimes save a little (+1.8 to +5.0 R at 3 of 5 checkpoints, 29 to 47 trades; -3.0 and -5.0 R at the other two). The user's second claim is already built into the rules: they let winners run to the clock exit or the trailing stop, and the earlier tracks found that taking profits sooner costs money (targets at 0.5 R kept 6-25 % of the expectancy, break-even at +1 R changed it by -36 % to +7 %) and that adding to winners gave nothing. Only 9.5 % of the losers had been 1 R ahead (22-23 % on ocm4 and orb gold). Holding winners even longer looked better on 5 of the 10 sleeves in the payoff lens's in-sample table (trades 1 R ahead held two more sessions: ocm4 +0.11 -> +0.25 R per trade, F1 eth +0.20 -> +0.41, F1 btc +0.34 -> +0.45, brk72 eth +0.21 -> +0.30, brk72 btc +0.26 -> +0.30) and worse or equal on noise30, orb gold, nq and GOLD_FRI_PM. When the signals lose (context lens, baseline trades, FP): breakouts taken just after their own volatility unit has expanded earn much less (highest vs lowest third of vol / 60-day median: brk72 btc +0.07 vs +0.62 R per trade, brk72 eth -0.06 vs +0.57, F1 btc +0.09 vs +0.77, F1 eth +0.07 vs +0.36, donch4h -0.01 vs +0.39, orb +0.13 vs +0.44), and crypto breakouts with a stop wide in % of the price lose (brk72 eth widest third -0.18 R per trade on 173 trades, negative in each year 2018-2021). No 2022+ row was read; the validation look is declared, not run.

The portfolio's in-sample gain (P0 -> P2: +0.152 -> +0.198 R per trade) comes mostly from adding the two orb crypto sleeves, i.e. more trades of a rule that was strong in 2018-2019, not from better trades of the ten: K1 alone moves the ten from +0.152 to +0.157 R per trade. On 2020-2021 alone the mean / sd of R per trade is 0.107 without and 0.106 with the changes.
K1 rests on its 2021 fold, which skips only because 2018 is in the expanding training window; once the context lens's search is counted, no null test puts it below 5 %.

The orb crypto sleeves: edge per trade halved between 2018-2019 and 2020-2021 (bitcoin about zero in 2021); 72-83 % of their R comes from positions held over the weekend, which the current hands close on Friday 23:50 server; ethusd would carry three sleeves and btcusd four for two positions per symbol (30 and 27 entries refused in the verifiers' runs); orb btcusd was not tradable at the 2018-2020 quoted spreads (+0.05 R per trade there); the two pairs are largely the same bet (weekly correlation 0.40) and correlate with the existing crypto sleeves; the ethusd FP spread is marked uncertain.

Ideal constant-stake account: 1 R per trade, no compounding, no minimum lot, no cap on simultaneous positions (the cluster lens's caps 6 / 2 remove 329 trades, -4.7 R, from the ten). The worst week grows from -12.5 to -16.9 R and the drawdown from 29.1 to 32.1 R because there are more trades; per unit of swing (weekly mean / sd 0.40 -> 0.46) it is better, in sample.

One trade per new sleeve still open at the end of 2021 is excluded (the lens counted it): 344 instead of 345 trades on ethusd, 375 instead of 376 on btcusd (-0.5 and -0.3 R); the gold donch4h and orb trades entered on 2021-12-31 are excluded the same way. The statements about holding winners longer quote the payoff lens's in-sample table before its attacks; those candidates (and the path and entry lenses) are judged in the other synthesis. If it keeps a change for brk72_24h_wd ethusd, at most one change may go forward on that sleeve.

The FP frames' spread uses a day-median shape that is not causal; K1's descriptor does not use the spread, but its training labels and every simulated fill do (the verifier bounds the effect at about 0.03 R for wide stops).
